desc:
The string pattern consists of lowercase letters. The string words is a list of lowercase words joined by single commas, for example "dog,cat,cat,dog" (it contains no spaces).

The words follow the pattern if there is a one-to-one correspondence between the letters of the pattern and the words: the i-th word is the word assigned to the letter pattern[i], the same letter always stands for the same word, and two different letters never stand for the same word. The number of words must also equal the length of the pattern.

pattern = "abba", words = "dog,cat,cat,dog"   result = true
pattern = "abba", words = "dog,cat,cat,fish"  result = false
pattern = "abba", words = "dog,dog,dog,dog"   result = false
pattern = "aaa",  words = "go,go"             result = false
constraints: words is 1 or more lowercase words of length 1 to 8, separated by single commas
hints: First compare the number of words with the length of the pattern.
Letters of the pattern must always meet the same word. But that alone is not enough: "ab" with "go,go" passes it.
Keep two dictionaries, letter → word and word → letter. When you see a pair, both dictionaries must agree with it (or be new).
editorial: Split the word list on commas. If the count differs from the pattern length the answer is false. Then scan the two sequences in parallel and keep a map from letters to words and a map from words back to letters. A pair (c, w) is consistent when c is unmapped or already mapped to w, and w is unmapped or already mapped back to c.

This is the same bijection check as for isomorphic strings, but one side consists of whole words. An equivalent trick replaces every symbol by the index of its first occurrence and compares the two index sequences. Both run in time linear in the input size.
